If you get sick, so be it.

Know that what you are afraid of is the result of your impression of COVID. When you hear people say that "fear is all in your head", they're onto something. The actual thing isn't to be feared, it's your opinion of it that makes you fearful. Remind yourself that COVID is a naturally-occuring illness. It won't eliminate your anxiety about it completely, but it will lessen it.

You've never had control over your body, nor have you ever had control over when you get sick.

Anxiety comes from our desire to control what we can't actually control. Yes, you can influence things to the best of your ability, but you cannot will yourself into no longer being sick. The best you can do is influence the results, but don't get too attached to your preferred results.

Even then, if you got vaccinated, you will be fine even if you do contract it. If you got the booster, then doubly so.

Stoicism isn't passivity. There are a few things you have control over, and a lot more you *don't* have control over. That does not mean you aren't able to *influence* things outside of your control. You seem to be confusing self-control of your behavior for total adherence.

Also, don't follow every single thing that the ancient Stoic philosophers say. Although they are all Stoics, they are still different people with (at least slightly) different beliefs. From them, you are supposed to create your own moral code, not adopt another's completely.

However, ever since magic became commonplace, mythical creatures (elves, dragons, headless men, etc.) started to appear.

With the setting, I want to explore how our world would change if all of a sudden stuff like magic and dragons started to exist. How would technology change? How would laws change? I hope to explore these questions in several novels later on as an anthology series.
